title: introduce-whatif-economics-simulator-and-safe-quant-rollout-cli
author: Maya Chen
description: Adds a tenant-level "what-if" economics simulator and a small CLI to run dry-run rollouts of quantization tiers and prefill/batching defaults. Motivation: customers ask for an easy, reproducible way to estimate unit economics before applying tenant defaults and to perform safe progressive quant rollouts. This PR implements a simulator that replays representative traces (sampled or uploaded), computes per-tenant token/cost/latency projections across candidate batch/cache/quant profiles, and produces guidance and safe fallback rules. It also adds a lightweight CLI (redwood econ-sim) for engineers and SREs to run local dry-runs, compare scenarios, and generate rollout manifests that can be applied by the operator. The simulator is conservative by default: it estimates 95th percentile latency impact, uses pessimistic (worst-case) KV cache hit assumptions unless trace contains explicit cache signals, and annotates risk factors for each recommended profile. Safe-quant rollout logic: supports staged canaries (percent-based traffic shifts), automatic rollback triggers (latency/quality/cost thresholds), and a embargo window for slow-roll updates. The rollout manifests can be executed via existing rollout controller with the new "econ-rollout" hook. Telemetry: emits new telemetry events (econ.sim.run, econ.sim.recommendation, econ.rollout.start/complete/abort) and adds dashboard panels in Console for scenario comparisons. Tests: unit tests for cost math, integration tests that run small-sample traces through the simulator, and e2e smoke tests for CLI->rollout manifest application. Backward compatibility: simulator only reads/export manifests and does not change live defaults until an operator applies a manifest. See related linear tasks ENG-4895 and PM-122 for design notes and UX mockups.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Ground-level question: are we assuming KV cache hit rate defaults per tenant? Please ensure defaults are explicit so operators understand conservatism.
Maya Chen (reply): We default to 10% optimistic hit and a 'pessimistic' run at 0% hit for risk annotation; updated docs to clarify and exposed --cache-assumption flag on CLI.
Luis Romero: CI flake on integration test; looks like trace fixture timestamp parsing was brittle. Suggest normalizing timezone parsing.
Maya Chen (reply): Fixed: trace parser normalizes to UTC and added fixtures. Re-ran CI and green.
Sofia Nguyen: Can we wire the rollout abort to existing SLO alerting so engineers see the same signals?
Maya Chen (reply): Yes, econ.rollout abort emits a standard alert label; added mapping in telemetry and ops runbook.
Code owner approval: Arjun Patel approved; Luis Romero approved after tests; Sofia Nguyen approved after runbook tweak.
release_notes: New CLI: 'redwood econ-sim' for tenant what-if economics simulations and a safe quant rollout manifest generator. Adds telemetry and Console panels for scenario comparison. Operators can preview cost/latency impact before applying tenant defaults.
